Solution: `5a6e8d40` (PR #268). Argument parsing moved out of the entry file into `source/mcp/args.ts`, which returns what the argument is rather than assuming it is a name: `--version`/`-v` print the version to stdout and exit 0, `--help`/`-h` print usage, any other `-`-prefixed argument is refused with exit 1, and only a bare argument reaches `applyActorNameArgument`.

Split out because the prelude in `index.ts` is unreachable from a unit test — it sets `process.env` and starts a server on import. `source/test/mcp-args.test.ts` covers it, including a case asserting no flag shape ever parses as a name. Also smoke-tested against the real entry point: `--version` prints `1.8.2`, `--bogus` exits 1.

stdout rather than `console.log`, which the prelude has already aliased to stderr — a version is worth piping.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: `DISCLOSURE_HOVER_BG` deleted; its two importers and the six inlined copies of the same literal (`CopyShaButton`, `FullscreenToggleButton`, `KebabMenu`, `IssueDetails`, `Button`, `DockButtons`) now read `GUI_THEME.hover`. `DiffStat`, `FileRow` and `DiffPanel` take `CODE_FONT` instead of `'ui-monospace, monospace'` — which also widens them to the full stack the rest of the app's code text uses.

On the near-misses [[4BBH20B]] raised: both are left alone, and deliberately. `TicketCard`'s 0.035 is the comment chip's *resting* ground — its hover is an accent tint — and `CodeSnippet`'s 0.03 is the caption bar's ground. `GUI_THEME.hover` is defined as what the pointer is over; neither is that, so they are not drift toward it. PR #270.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: the assertion is now three, each with its own budget — the row is waited for by subject (`/^add notes/`), then its accessible name (`add notes +3 -0`), then `aria-expanded`. The single 10s timeout was covering both the tab opening and the diff stat arriving from git, and reported "element not found" for whichever half was late.

Verified 18/18 under `--repeat-each=6 --workers=4` on a loaded machine, against ~1-in-13 before. PR #270.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: added a `halfyear` scope between `month` and `year`. Two calls worth recording:

- **180 days, not 182.5.** Six of the `month` scope (30 days) rather than half of `year` (365), so paging back by a half-year lands on the same boundaries the month scope steps on.
- **Labelled "6 months".** Every other scope's button label is its id capitalized; `Halfyear` is not a word anyone wants, so `scopeButtonLabel` special-cases this one. The pager reads "Last 180 days", matching "Last 30 days" / "Last 365 days".

No axis work needed — `chooseSegmentUnit` picks off the duration, so 180 days gets month segments on its own. PR #270.
